steps.path: The pencil at the right end of the status bar
steps.headline: Labelled cards, a switch on each row, a hint under each name; the four fixed items are one line.
steps.changed: Tick boxes became switches on the right. Each (i) became a one-line hint under the name (the first sentence of what the (i) said; its "Best for" advice is gone). "Always on" is one sentence at the top. The theme cycle is a fold under the Theme row.
steps.notice: Switching something on or off works like the switches in Settings.
steps.risk: Taller rows: the menu scrolls further.

steps.path: The pencil at the end of the chips above the message box
steps.headline: Each chip shows its whole message, and the reorder grip and edit pencil are always visible.
steps.changed: Rows sit in a "Your chips (7 of 10)" card; each shows the name with its message under it (up to two lines). Clicking a row still opens it to edit; dragging the grip still reorders, but the grip and pencil no longer hide until you hover. "+ Add Chip" is an outlined "+ Add a chip" button.
steps.notice: You can see what each chip sends, and that chips can be reordered.
steps.risk: On a phone the row itself is the drag handle, as before.

steps.path: The tag chip in the status bar
steps.headline: Tags & note is two labelled cards, Tags and Note, in the standard popup frame; "Manage tags…" is gone.
steps.changed: Each tag has a "…" at the right. Archived tags are in a fold at the bottom of the Tags card. The popup now uses the same header and close button as every other popup.
steps.notice: Everything about tags in one place.
steps.risk: So far only this popup has it; the close-session prompt and Resume's Organize menu still use "Manage tags…" until you approve this.

steps.path: The tag chip in the status bar → the "…" on a tag
steps.headline: The "…" opens that tag's colour, name, Archive and Delete right under it, instead of the separate Manage tags popup.
steps.changed: Before: Manage tags, a second popup with a name box and two buttons on every tag. After: the same controls, for one tag at a time, inside Tags & note. Delete still asks "Delete?" before deleting.
steps.notice: Renaming a tag no longer means leaving the popup you were in.
steps.risk: Delete is one click from the tick you use every day (it still needs a second click to confirm).
